svg.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: Operix Core MVP - Entity Relationship Diagram (PostgreSQL, multi-tenant)
svg.desc: Core MVP database for Operix. Every tenant-owned table carries factory_id; foreign keys between tenant tables are composite (factory_id, id). Redesigned layout: same tables, columns, keys and relationships as the original.
svg.text: PostgreSQL - multi-tenant (shared schema, factory_id + composite foreign keys + Row-Level Security) - 20 tables - crow's-foot notation

g.text: How tenant isolation is enforced (database level)
1. Every tenant table has factory_id NOT NULL -> factories.id (amber rows).
Global catalogs without RLS: users, roles, permissions, role_permissions, auth_tokens.
2. Each parent has UNIQUE (factory_id, id); every FK between tenant tables is composite:
(factory_id, parent_id) -> parent (factory_id, id). A child row cannot reference another
factory's camera, zone, rule, sensor, event or incident (lines show the single-column link).
3. Row-Level Security (ENABLE + FORCE) on every tenant table:
The API sets app.factory_id per transaction after verifying factory_memberships;
the application DB role has no BYPASSRLS.
4. Evidence keys start with f/<factory_id>/ and signed URLs are issued after the same check.
Ingestion services derive factory_id from the camera / sensor, never from the payload.

text.font-family: ui-monospace, 'SF Mono', Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

g.text: Enum types (e.g. event_type) are PostgreSQL ENUMs.
All keys are UUID; time columns are timestamptz (UTC).
- No frames, no per-frame detections, no raw video.
- No continuous tracking: only events that passed
the rules, plus incidents that need a human.
- Evidence = files in object storage; the DB keeps
- Sensor readings: one row per sampling interval,
